key_highlights: ASX posts fourth consecutive losing week as rising bond yields pressure equities; 'will bonds crash stocks' debate intensifies
RBA signals continued hikes despite sharp unemployment jump, trapping households in an interest-rate pincer
AUD experiences a 'trapdoor' move, weakening materially against USD
Australian house prices over halfway to largest 40-year decline; Victorian unemployment leads national deterioration
Over half of renters now financially stressed; consumer confidence under pressure
Mining exploration active: Zenith six-for-six WA gold hits, Aurum 155g/t West Africa, Rio2 Peruvian copper drill, Auric high-grade WA gold
$2.7B small-cap cap raise wave keeps ASX brokers busy; Micro-X, Arrow Minerals, Mamba lead runners
Star's Sydney casino licence remains suspended, weighing on gaming/entertainment sector
Data centre energy demand boom flagged as potential energy supply risk
Geopolitical tensions: Ukraine-Russia drone strikes, China-US friction add macro uncertainty

sectors.trend: Exploration activity robust across gold (Zenith, Aurum, Auric, Kuniko) and copper (Rio2). Small-cap cap raises ($2.7B) signal capital-hungry pipeline but dilution risk. Large caps (BHP, RIO, FMG) face headwind from AUD weakness and softening Chinese demand signals.
sectors.implications: Exploration names offer asymmetric upside but high dilution risk. Major miners pressured by weaker AUD and China trade tensions. Gold miners benefit from safe-haven flows amid geopolitical risk.

sectors.trend: RBA hawkish stance despite unemployment spike supports net interest margins but raises credit-loss concerns. Rising bond yields compress bank equity valuations. Renters' financial stress (50%+) foreshadows mortgage arrears risk.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face margin tailwinds but credit-cycle risk rising. REITs (property lenders) under pressure from falling house prices and high cap rates.

sectors.trend: Data centre boom creating structural energy demand but flagged as potential supply 'bust'. AGL, CSG, and energy infrastructure names in focus. Coal and LNG exporters monitor China demand signals.
sectors.implications: Energy infrastructure and renewables play benefit from data centre load. Traditional coal/LNG exporters face China-related demand uncertainty.

sectors.trend: Renter stress, unemployment rise, and rate pincer squeeze household budgets. WES.AX, WOW.AX face margin pressure. Bentley EV launch ($325k) signals premium EV competition. Coke/fast-food beverage innovation signals consumer trade-down.
sectors.implications: Defensive consumer staples (WES, WOW) relatively resilient but growth constrained. Discretionary spend under pressure.

sectors.trend: Medicare data breach prompts AI safety legislation calls. US AI/tech momentum (Nvidia, AMD, Zscaler) provides global sentiment support but limited direct ASX exposure. Data centre energy demand links to ASX energy names.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX remain defensive anchors. ASX tech exposure limited; indirect benefit via data centre energy demand.

sectors.trend: House prices over halfway to 40-year decline. CBD tower listed at $40m. Dusty Martin $20m portfolio haircut. Star casino licence suspended. Structural oversupply and high cap rates pressure valuations.
sectors.implications: Property REITs (GPW.AX, DGL.AX, ICPS.AX) face falling asset values and rising refinancing costs. Gaming/entertainment REITs hit by Star suspension.

key_themes: RBA rate pincer: hiking into rising unemployment creates stagflationary risk for equities
AUD trapdoor: currency weakness supports miners' AUD revenue but signals capital outflows
Bond yield spike: fourth losing week driven by rising yields; duration risk to growth equities
Housing correction: 40-year low trajectory pressures banks, REITs, and construction
Mining exploration wave: gold and copper drill results positive but cap-raise dilution risk
Geopolitical risk premium: Ukraine strikes, China-US tensions elevate safe-haven demand
Energy transition stress: data centre demand vs supply constraints

risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight short-duration bonds and dividend-paying defensives; underweight rate-sensitive growth and REITs
Hedge AUD exposure; favour miners with USD/contracted revenue; monitor RBA intervention signals
Reduce REIT and construction exposure; monitor bank NIM vs credit-loss trajectory
Maintain 10-15% gold allocation; diversify away from China-exposed miners
Avoid sub-$50m cap names with repeated raises; focus on funded, de-risked exploration assets

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Energy supply constraint from data centre demand
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor AGL/CSG capacity expansion; watch for government energy policy response

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold miners and exploration names amid geopolitical risk and AUD weakness
opportunities.rationale: Zenith six-for-six WA hits, Aurum 155g/t, Auric high-grade results confirm pipeline; safe-haven flows support gold

opportunities.recommendation: Selective copper exposure via Rio2 and large-cap miners
opportunities.rationale: Rio2 Peruvian drill assault and global electrification demand support copper; AUD weakness boosts AUD-denominated earnings

opportunities.recommendation: Defensive healthcare and consumer staples positioning
opportunities.rationale: CSL, SGH, WES, WOW offer earnings visibility amid rate pincer and consumer stress

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce REIT and property exposure; trim rate-sensitive growth
defensive_moves.rationale: 40-year house price decline, rising cap rates, Star licence suspension, and bond yield spike create multi-factor headwind

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge AUD and reduce China-exposed mining weight
defensive_moves.rationale: AUD trapdoor and China-US friction create dual currency and demand risk for iron ore/coal exporters

defensive_moves.recommendation: Avoid undiluted small-cap miners with repeated cap raises
defensive_moves.rationale: $2.7B cap raise wave signals dilution risk; only fund de-risked, near-production assets

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to extend weakness into Q4 2026. Fourth losing week driven by bond yield spike and RBA hawkish bias. AUD weakness provides partial offset for miners but broad-based selling likely continues. Key watch: whether unemployment data triggers RBA pause or further hikes. Expect 3-5% further index decline risk.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautious. Housing correction and rate pincer weigh on consumer and financials. Mining exploration pipeline (gold, copper) offers selective upside. Energy transition and data centre demand create structural tailwinds for utilities. Recovery contingent on RBA pivot and global demand stabilisation.
